title: A Simple Way To Build Rapport With Challenging Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes a strategy that builds behavior-influencing rapport with even the most guarded or difficult students: taking a genuine, unconditional interest in them as people, with no hidden agenda or expected outcome. He warns that students can immediately sense any ulterior motive behind a teacher's curiosity and will shut down further if they detect one, so the approach must be built on small, low-pressure moments of genuine curiosity rather than concentrated one-on-one time or the use of praise and flattery to draw students out. He offers example questions a teacher might casually ask and explains that the law of reciprocity eventually causes students to become curious about the teacher in return, gradually drawing them into engaging with the rest of the class as well. Linsin frames the teacher as a bridge that helps isolated or difficult students become genuine, valued members of the classroom community.
points: Genuine, unconditional interest in a student as a person—without any hidden agenda—builds rapport even with the most guarded students.
Students can detect an ulterior motive behind adult curiosity and will shut down further if they sense one.
The approach works best through small, low-pressure moments rather than concentrated one-on-one attention.
Praise and flattery should be avoided when trying to draw a student out, since they signal a hidden agenda.
The law of reciprocity eventually causes students to become curious about the teacher and more engaged with the rest of the class.
quotes: There is a strategy that builds strong, behavior-influencing rapport with virtually any student.
It’s about your genuine desire to get to know them, nothing more.
But you must have no ulterior motive, no hidden agenda, no strings attached. Because if you do, if you think of it as a strategy to get something from them, they’ll know it.
Be direct and refrain from using praise or flattery to try to get them to open up. This is a common tactic that communicates loud and clear that you do, in fact, have an ulterior motive.
In time, you’ll discover common interests and be drawn into wanting to learn more and more about them. Inevitably, they’ll also become curious about you.
